title: Stale API-key -> org mapping after fast-path cache invalidation regression (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported cross-tenant authorization anomalies after a recent runtime optimization that introduced a fast-path for org-scoped API key lookup. Symptom: requests authenticated with a valid API key were intermittently routed with the wrong org-scoping (tenant A requests appearing as tenant B), leading to transient access to resources outside of the intended org. Affected environments: Hosted API (rare), Dedicated pools (observed during scale-up), Private/VPC (high frequency for one on-prem customer).

Timeline & detection: On 2026-03-09 we received an escalation from a Private deployment customer with data access observations. On 2026-03-09 evening, SRE correlated higher-than-normal 401->200 recoveries in the auth proxy and opened an incident. Initial mitigations (2026-03-09 22:00): revoke suspect API key, toggle feature-flag disabling fast-path on the customer cluster.

Root cause hypothesis: The fast-path optimization added a two-tier lookup: local in-memory map (fast) backed by memcached/multi-tenant mapping. During org rebinds (API key reassignment, org migrations, or rotation events) we failed to invalidate the in-memory entry consistently across instances. A race between the async rebind job and token refresh paths allowed a stale mapping to be used for a small window. Additionally, a fallback path to global issuer used KMS alias resolution which, under certain HSM key aliasing, returned legacy metadata leading to wrong tenant IDs. The combo produced cross-tenant acceptance when (1) a request hit an instance with stale in-memory entry and (2) token refresh was allowed within the grace window.

Reproduction steps: (1) Create two orgs A and B; (2) Create API key K under A; (3) Trigger org-rebind to move K to B using the internal org-migration job; (4) Simultaneously send high-rate requests that exercise token refresh and the fast-path lookup. Observed: a subset of requests accepted with tenant=A mapping then later with tenant=B.

Impact: Customer-reported data exposure risk (high sensitivity for regulated customers). One enterprise Private customer observed list endpoints returning ~0.2% foreign org items for a 10 minute window during migration. Several Dedicated customers saw transient incorrect telemetry and increased support tickets.

Mitigation & proposed fix: 1) Emergency mitigation: feature-flag disable fast-path and force authoritative lookup path (done 2026-03-09 23:15 across affected clusters). 2) Patch: ensure atomic invalidation across instances by using memcached CAS + pub/sub invalidation channel and extend token refresh revocation window tightening. 3) KMS alias handling: add deterministic alias-to-tenant mapping and fallback hardening for HSM responses. 4) Add end-to-end test harness that simulates concurrent rebind + refresh. 5) Rollout plan: cherry-pick patch to runtime-1.20.3, small canary (1 Dedicated pool + affected Private customer), monitor for 48h before full roll.

Testing & QA: unit tests for cache invalidation, integration test against local memcached+pubsub, chaos test for org-rebind concurrency. Add regression suite to CI with simulated HSM metadata permutations.

Customer communication: We drafted an incident notice for affected customers describing root cause, mitigation, and planned timeline. Affected customer success reps have been briefed and incident-owner will run a sync call with the largest impacted on-prem customer on 2026-03-13.

Links & artifacts: Postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ENG-34172-auth-incident, PR with fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9123, hotfix build: gs://redwood-builds/runtime/1.20.3-hotfix-34172.tar.gz, incident channel: https://chat.redwood.ai/archives/C12345/p1678901234000, diagnostics dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/auth/tenant-mapping?orgId=1&var-job=fastpath
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Incident triaged. Fast-path feature-flag toggled off for all Dedicated and Private clusters. Initial customer mitigation executed; working with SRE to push hotfix.

2026-03-11 - Ravi Suresh: Root cause narrowed to inconsistent invalidation in in-memory fast-path cache + HSM alias fallback. Drafted patch to introduce pub/sub invalidation and tighten token refresh grace window. Preparing PR.
2026-03-11 - Jen Ortiz (SRE): Deployed canary hotfix to one Dedicated pool; observed no cross-tenant mappings in 6h window. Telemetry shows expected drop in stale-cache hits (from 0.8% to <0.01%).

2026-03-12 - Code review (ENG): PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9123 created. Requested changes: add CI chaos test and add metric for pubsub invalidation latency. Assigned to @ravi for follow-up.
2026-03-12 - Customer success note: Preparing communication for impacted customers. Legal notified due to potential data exposure; coordinating scoreboard for regulatory reporting if required.
